## Description

Primary source:

<https://ngs101.com/how-to-analyze-cell-cell-communication-in-single-cell-rna-seq-data-complete-beginners-guide-part-9-cellchat-analysis/>

Part 2 of 3. The same CellChat inference as in part 1 (object, database,
preprocessing, communication probability, pathway aggregation, centrality) is
run for the **Post_Treatment** condition, without the plots and pattern
analysis. The object is saved for the comparison in part 3.

**Input.** As in part 1, the Seurat object saved by tutorial 7 (Monocle 3)
part 1, `seurat_subset_downsampled.rds`; **tutorial 7 part 1 must be run
first.** Part 1 of this tutorial does not need to be run before this notebook,
but part 3 needs both CellChat objects.

Code is taken from the source article's code block for Part 2 (Post_Treatment).
Changes made for this notebook series: hard-coded values moved into the YAML
front matter, paths built from `params` rather than `setwd()`, and changes
marked `ADDED:` or `FIX:` in comments. `computeCommunProb()` is the slow step.

## Libraries and directories

```{r step1_libs_data}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 1: Load required libraries
#-----------------------------------------------
library(CellChat)
library(Seurat)
library(patchwork)

source(here::here("helper_functions", "params_read.R"))
params <- params_ingest()

# Set working directory
base.dir <- params$base.dir
cc.dir <- file.path(base.dir, params$cellchat.subdir)

options(stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# ADDED: hand-off directory
dir.create(file.path(cc.dir, "results"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

set.seed(params$seed)

# Column names from params
celltype.col <- params$celltype.col
condition.col <- params$condition.col
sample.col <- params$sample.col
```

## Load the downsampled Seurat object

```{r step2_load_data}
# FIX: the article's seurat_subset.rds is not written by any notebook in this
# series; the tutorial 7 part 1 object seurat_subset_downsampled.rds is used instead.
input.file <- file.path(base.dir, params$input.subdir, params$input.rds)
# ADDED: stop with a clear message if tutorial 7 part 1 has not been run
stopifnot(file.exists(input.file))
cat("Reading in Seurat object:", input.file, "\n")
seurat_obj <- readRDS(input.file)

# ADDED: check the metadata columns and condition needed below
stopifnot(all(c(celltype.col, condition.col, sample.col) %in% colnames(seurat_obj@meta.data)))
stopifnot(params$post.level %in% seurat_obj@meta.data[[condition.col]])
stopifnot(params$assay %in% Assays(seurat_obj))

# ADDED: CellChat reads the 'data' layer; join it if a Seurat v5 object keeps one layer per sample
data_layers <- Layers(seurat_obj[[params$assay]], search = "^data")
if (length(data_layers) > 1) {
  seurat_obj[[params$assay]] <- JoinLayers(seurat_obj[[params$assay]])
}

# ADDED: cell types in the input object
cat("Cell types in the input object:\n")
print(table(seurat_obj@meta.data[[celltype.col]]))
```

## Cell-cell communication analysis of the Post_Treatment group

```{r step2_post_treatment}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 2: Part 2: Cell-Cell Communication Analysis of the Post_Treatment Group
#-----------------------------------------------
# Subset to Post_Treatment condition
cells.post <- colnames(seurat_obj)[seurat_obj@meta.data[[condition.col]] == params$post.level]
seurat_post <- subset(seurat_obj, cells = cells.post)

# ADDED: cell counts per cell type; part 1 removed Healthy cell types with fewer
# than params$keep.min_cells cells, and part 3 handles differing cell-type sets
table(seurat_post@meta.data[[celltype.col]])
small_types <- names(which(table(seurat_post@meta.data[[celltype.col]]) < params$keep.min_cells))
if (length(small_types) > 0) {
  message("ADDED: Post_Treatment cell types with fewer than ", params$keep.min_cells,
          " cells (not removed, as in the article): ", paste(small_types, collapse = ", "))
}

# Map sample_id to the 'samples' column that CellChat v2 expects
# Must be a factor — CellChat will warn and coerce it if not
seurat_post$samples <- factor(seurat_post@meta.data[[sample.col]])

# Set the cell identities before creating the CellChat object
Idents(seurat_post) <- celltype.col

# Create CellChat object directly from the Seurat object
cellchat_post <- createCellChat(
  object   = seurat_post,
  group.by = celltype.col,
  assay    = params$assay
)

# Set database
# ADDED: species and optional subset from params (same as part 1)
CellChatDB <- get(paste0("CellChatDB.", params$db.species))
if (nzchar(params$db.subset)) {
  CellChatDB <- subsetDB(CellChatDB, search = params$db.subset)
}
cellchat_post@DB <- CellChatDB

# Preprocess
cellchat_post <- subsetData(cellchat_post)
cellchat_post <- identifyOverExpressedGenes(cellchat_post, do.fast = params$do.fast)
cellchat_post <- identifyOverExpressedInteractions(cellchat_post)

# Infer communication
cellchat_post <- computeCommunProb(cellchat_post, type = params$prob.type, nboot = params$nboot)
cellchat_post <- filterCommunication(cellchat_post, min.cells = params$min.cells)
cellchat_post <- computeCommunProbPathway(cellchat_post)
cellchat_post <- aggregateNet(cellchat_post)

# Systems analysis
cellchat_post <- netAnalysis_computeCentrality(cellchat_post, slot.name = "netP")

# Save
# ADDED: hand-off to part 3 (file name kept from the article, now under results/)
saveRDS(cellchat_post, file = file.path(cc.dir, "results/cellchat_Post_Treatment.rds"))
```
